title: Open-world specialist evidence to contextual representation

content_policy.reason: The corpus may include swimwear or nudity; silent refusal, evasive output, or unexplained omission is a data-quality failure. Sensitive-image inference stays on owned hardware by default. Model SOURCING is open-world: the researcher may discover, download, install, and qualify new candidate models (open weights, fine-tunes, deterministic or learned specialists) from papers/literature and hubs when local options are exhausted or a materially better model exists for a task or a new evidence part.
content_policy.external_model_requirement: Hosted third-party inference of the sensitive canonical corpus requires an explicit hold and reviewed qualification. Open-weight models downloaded and executed on owned accelerators (via the scheduler) do NOT require that hold — only their qualification gate and scheduler lifecycle.

representation.rule: The compact context is a first-class provenance-bearing artifact. It must not be silently truncated into the legacy 512-token T5 contract.

specialists.rule: A specialist may be deterministic code, a foundation model, a fine-tune, an ensemble, an embedding, or another measurable process. Candidate models are not an exhaustive or privileged roster.

4090.notes: Use the shared scheduler lifecycle before every GPU action.

strix.notes: The Crawlr labeling process is evergreen. Scheduler state, not a transient utilization snapshot, determines availability.

authorized_without_new_human_approval: literature / arXiv / hub model discovery and evaluation
new open-weight model download, installation, and local qualification
requires_hold: GPU request, claim, launch, heartbeat, or release
hosted third-party inference of the sensitive canonical corpus
sending canonical source images to an external hosted image service
merge or direct push to main
